we propose to learn a mapping from a low- to high- dimensional space, which is a generalization of normalizing flows.

(1) we propose a new class of injective flows, rectangular flows, that are more expressive than previous injective flows, (2) we propose two novel methods to compute the gradient of the volume-change term of injective flows that can be used to train rectangular flows, (3) we empirically show that rectangular flows trained with our proposed methods outperform existing injective flows in manifold learning and density modeling
we provide a general framework to learn the manifold structure and the corresponding density of the data on the learned manifold.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn distributions on manifolding data in a fully differentiable manner without any assumptions about the underlying manifold.
it is possible to perform tractable manifold learning with normalizing flows, which is an important step in the direction of using such models for unsupervised representation learning.

, in the case where we have no prior knowledge about the manifold on which data live, we can still learn the manifold and its corresponding distribution using normalizing flows, and do so in a tractable manner.
